inline_comments.comment: `projectInfo.renderer` is the full package name (e.g. `@storybook/react`), not the short renderer name. Interpolating it as `@storybook/${renderer}` produces `@storybook/@storybook/react` in the generated instructions, which will confuse AI agents trying to write stories. `getStorybookInfo` returns both a short `renderer` field (`'react'`) and a `rendererPackage` field (`'@storybook/react'`); the PR routes `rendererPackage` through. Either thread the short `renderer` value through `ProjectInfo` and use it here, or strip the prefix: `projectInfo.renderer?.replace('@storybook/', '') || 'react'`.

When the framework is not `@storybook/react-vite` the function returns silently with no output and no error message. A user running `storybook ai prepare` on an Angular, Vue, or Svelte project will see a blank prompt and have no idea why. At minimum log something like `logger.warn(\`AI setup is currently only supported for @storybook/react-vite. Your framework (${projectInfo.framework}) is not yet supported.\`)` before returning.

`await import('../../cli-storybook/src/ai')` is a deep relative import that crosses package boundaries directly into `@storybook/cli`'s source directory. Per the project rule, code in one monorepo package must import from another package's public export, not its internal source paths. Replace with a static import from the package's public entry point (`import { aiPrepare } from '@storybook/cli'` or the mapped internal identifier) and remove the dynamic import wrapper.

`std-env` is imported here but is not listed in `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json` under `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. It appears only in `code/core/package.json` as a dev dependency. Without an explicit declaration in this package's manifest, resolution is fragile across package managers and will fail in clean installs. Add `std-env` to `devDependencies` in `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json`.

`resolvedAgent` is computed here in `preAction` (`options.agent ?? isAgent`) to conditionally enable log writing, but the resolved value is never written back to `options`. Then in the action handler (line ~129) the exact same expression is evaluated a second time and finally stored. This double-computation is subtle and can diverge if `isAgent` is ever non-deterministic. Store the resolved value back to `options.agent` in `preAction` (i.e., `options.agent = resolvedAgent`) so the single source of truth is set once.

The project rule for mocking `process` properties says to use a getter spy (`vi.spyOn(process.stdout, 'isTTY', 'get').mockReturnValue(...)`) rather than `Object.defineProperty`. Getter spies integrate automatically with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` / `vi.resetAllMocks()`, are reliably reversible across Node versions, and prevent mock state from leaking into subsequent tests. This pattern appears in every `Object.defineProperty(process.stdout, 'isTTY', ...)` call throughout this file; all of them should be converted.

The mock queue comments are reversed relative to the actual execution order. Looking at the code path for a new user with a recommended install: `promptAiSetup` is called first (consuming the first `mockResolvedValueOnce`), and there is no longer a separate 'continue without test' confirm prompt in the current implementation — `isTestFeatureAvailable` now returns a boolean directly without prompting. The first mock labeled `// continue without test` is actually consumed by AI setup; the second mock labeled `// AI setup` is never consumed. Update comments to reflect the real call order and remove the unused queued value.

`getPrompts` builds an empty array, pushes one item, then returns it. Since it always returns exactly one prompt, just return the array literal directly: `return [{ name: 'setup', ... }]`. The intermediate variable adds no clarity.

The JSDoc says "Represents a skill category that can be expanded in the future" but the interface is named `AiPrompt` and the whole `skill` concept was renamed to `ai`/`prepare` in this PR. The comment is stale and will confuse future readers. Update it to describe what `AiPrompt` actually is: an agent-facing prompt definition with a name, description, and instructions string.

`import { dedent } from 'ts-dedent'` is a third-party import placed after the relative imports (`./generators`, `./services/*`). Per the project's ESLint import-order configuration, third-party imports must come before relative imports. Move this line up to the third-party block alongside `ts-dedent`.

`promptAiSetup` returns `true` by default whenever `skipPrompt` is `true` (non-interactive mode, `--yes` flag, CI). This silently opts users into installing `@storybook/addon-mcp` without any consent signal in automated pipelines. A comment explaining the intentional opt-in default (e.g., `// In non-interactive mode AI setup is enabled by default`) would clarify this policy for future maintainers and reviewers.

general_comments.comment: The `ProjectInfo.renderer` field is populated from `data.rendererPackage` (a full npm package name like `@storybook/react`), but the field is named and described as if it holds a short renderer identifier. This naming mismatch propagates the wrong value into `getCsfExample`, creating the broken `@storybook/@storybook/react` import path. Consider storing the short renderer name (available from `data.renderer` in `getStorybookInfo`) in `ProjectInfo.renderer` instead of the package name, and adding a separate `rendererPackage` field if the full name is needed for other purposes. That way future prompt-building code cannot accidentally misuse the full package name as an identifier fragment.

The framework restriction in `ai/index.ts` (`if (projectInfo.framework !== '@storybook/react-vite') return`) hardcodes a single supported framework as a magic string comparison. As more frameworks are supported, this pattern will require multiple string comparisons or an allowlist. Consider defining a `SUPPORTED_AI_FRAMEWORKS` constant (e.g., `const SUPPORTED_AI_FRAMEWORKS = ['@storybook/react-vite'] as const`) and using `includes`, which also makes it easy to spot and extend in the future.

No automated tests cover the new `ai/index.ts` or `ai/prompt.ts` modules (the PR checklist has no boxes checked for stories, unit tests, integration tests, or e2e tests). At a minimum, a unit test for `generateMarkdownOutput` / `getPrompts` would catch regressions like the broken renderer import path and the silent no-op for unsupported frameworks. Consider adding tests before merging.
